narrative: Your promotion was denied because the model estimates a 64% chance that you will leave your job, and the organization treats that risk as a reason not to invest in a promotion. The strongest factor in your case is your relatively short overall work experience of one to five years; this actually pushed the prediction toward staying, since about half of employees predicted to stay also have that experience level. However, it was outweighed by two factors pointing toward leaving. You reported having other job opportunities, which is unusual among employees predicted to stay—only about a quarter had such opportunities—and that strongly suggests you may exit. Your sector, classified as “other,” also nudged the prediction toward leaving, though it was less influential than the opportunities. The model therefore sees enough flight risk to deny advancement, even though your experience length alone would have favored stability. To reverse this, discuss with your manager what would make you stay: clearer promotion pathways, recognition, fair pay or bonuses, training, and a realistic view of your outside options. The organization should also review whether your role can meet your needs and whether the denied promotion itself is contributing to the risk. Gender, age, and health issues were not used in the prediction.
